title: Clifford Minutes #541
snippet:
Clifford Minutes #541

Crypto Newsletters 
•• Polymarket has entered a fully fee-based era, and its annual revenue may exceed $400 million

•• Research Roundup Newsletter (March 2026): We present to you our latest issue of Research Roundup, featuring our deep dives into the prediction markets and February’s market review and outlook

•• The Rise of the Autonomous Wallet: This report outlines the 2026 transition from human-managed DeFi to an agentic economy, driven by machine-native financial infrastructure

•• Aave (AAVE) launched its V4 iteration on Ethereum, designed to expand decentralized lending into real-world credit markets

•• Ethereum Foundation staked an additional $42 million in ETH, demonstrating its continued commitment to securing the network and validating the long-term utility of Proof of Stake

•• LayerZero integrated with the Canton Network as its first interoperability protocol, and aims to streamline asset and data movement between institutional private blockchains and public Network

•• Circle Wrapped Bitcoin is coming; Backed 1:1 by BTC and readily verifiable onchain

•• Riot Platforms, one of the largest Bitcoin miners in the US, sold 500 BTC, worth approximately $34.13 million today

•• Franklin Templeton and Ondo Finance (ONDO) partnered to launch five tokenized ETFs, enabling non-U.S. investors in Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America to trade U.S. equities, bonds, and gold 24/7 via crypto wallets.

•• MARA sold 15,133 BTC between March 4 and March

title: I asked the CEO of one the top trading firms "how to become more financially literate".
snippet:
I asked the CEO of one the top trading firms "how to become more financially literate".

At the time, I was an incoming  quant trader and he was a fellow MIT alum.

His only recommendation... @matt_levine's Money Stuff! 

"Single best financial writer out there. If you read his newsletter five days a week for six months, you will learn an enormous amount. This is probably 1000x more useful than like, some random textbook or a podcast or whatever."

It's a quick, funny, easy-to-understand daily digest and so crucial for ANYONE (quant or non quant) to truly understand how our money and markets work.

I have yet to find any other newsletters worth the daily effort!

title: Clifford Minutes #542
snippet:
Clifford Minutes #542

Crypto Newsletters
•• Coinbase received conditional approval from the OCC for a national trust bank charter - not a commercial bank, no deposits, no fractional reserve banking

•• Drift was exploited for $285M on April 1 in the largest DeFi hack of 2026 and the second-largest in Solana history behind the $326M Wormhole hack in 2022

•• The Ethereum Foundation staked 45,034 ETH worth ~$93M Friday, bringing its total staked position to ~69,500 ETH, nearly completing the 70,000 ETH target it announced in February

•• The Bank of Canada published a report on Aave

•• US oil prices surge above $114/barrel as US market futures officially reopen after the 3-day weekend

•• Bitcoin closed Q1 2026 as its worst quarter since early 2018, shedding 22% as war, tariffs, and a hawkish Fed drove prices lower

•• Pavel Durov observes that Telegram bans in Iran and Russia failed to push users toward government surveillance apps

•• New Attorney General Todd Blanche held Bitcoin but continued prosecuting crypto software developers under his tenure as deputy AG; Trump fired Pam Bondi and elevated Blanche to run the DOJ last week

•• First on-chain robot-to-robot commerce transaction through x402 on @Base with @USDC as the agent currency

•• Six-month operation: attackers posed as a quant firm at crypto events starting October 2025, cultivating trust with Drift contributors in person before accessing admin keys via social engineering
